Grant-funded professional military education and training, in the United States and abroad, for foreign military personnel and related civilians. Added to the [Foreign Assistance Act](faa-1961.qmd) in 1976, it aims at professionalization, civilian control of the military, and respect for human rights as well as technical skill, and it builds long-term ties with future military leaders.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 90 Stat. 732](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/90/732){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 2347 and following](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2347?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 541(a): the President may furnish military education and training to military and related civilian personnel of foreign countries, on a reimbursable basis whenever feasible.
- Civilians, including officials outside defense ministries, legislators, and nongovernmental participants, qualify when training serves defense resource management, civilian control of the military, counternarcotics cooperation, or military justice and human rights (often called Expanded IMET).
- Training may be at U.S. military schools other than the service academies, in special courses, or through orientation visits.
- Sec. 541(b): countries that buy training with FMF are charged a rate comparable to grant IMET.
- Recipient units and individuals are subject to [Leahy Laws](leahy-laws.qmd) vetting.

## Why it matters

IMET is small in dollars but large in reach: it puts foreign officers through U.S. staff colleges and war colleges, and its graduates often rise to senior command. It is also among the first programs suspended when a partner's military seizes power under the [coup restriction](sec7008-coup.qmd) and among the first restored, which makes it a frequent subject of country-specific conditions.

## Current status

In force. Funded each year in Title IV of the State-foreign operations appropriations act. Check current status.

[Last checked November 24, 2026.]{.checked}

## Funding and administration

- **Account.** International Military Education and Training, Title IV (International Security Assistance) in the [State-foreign ops appropriations](sfops-approps-annual.qmd).
- **Run by.** The State Department, which sets country allocations, and the Defense Department, which runs the training through the Defense Security Cooperation Agency and the military departments.
- **Committees.** Authorizing, House Foreign Affairs and Senate Foreign Relations; appropriations, the House and Senate subcommittees for State and foreign operations.
